newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Thirteen journalists hurt in Arab-Israeli clash.
newsitem.headline: Thirteen journalists hurt in Arab-Israeli clash.

text.p: Thirteen journalists were among hundreds wounded on the frontlines of violent clashes between Palestinians and Israeli troops in which more than 50 people were killed in two days.

Two Israeli journalists were wounded on Thursday, one critically, when Palestinian police mistook for Israeli snipers a three-man television team from Israel's Second Channel perched atop a concrete tower in Gaza.

"We climbed up a concrete tower to film the start of demonstrations and stone-throwing," soundman Yaniv Shmueli told Channel Two while trapped on the tower at Erez checkpoint between Israel and Palestinian-ruled Gaza.
Shmueli said Palestinian policemen opened fire on the three from two directions while Israeli soldiers returned fire at Palestinian forces.

He said cameraman Haim Asyas was shot in the stomach and hand and reporter Yosi Endor took a bullet to the leg. Shmueli said he stopped Asyas' flow of blood and the three remained on the tower for close to two hours until medics came up to treat the wounded.
"Two medics came up -- one medic who came up the ladder immediately took a bullet in the leg and went back down," he told Channel Two.
Shmueli said the two wounded were later evacuated by crane.
CBS cameraman Issa Freij was critically wounded when hit in the chest by a live bullet near Ramallah in the West Bank, witnesses said. Freij was in serious condition at Ramallah hospital.

Mohammad Saadi, a reporter for the Palestinian Broadcasting Corpotation (PBC) was seriously wounded when hit in the stomach by a rubber bullet also near Ramallah. PBC said he was in surgery in Ramallah hospital.
Reuters cameraman Shams Odeh was shot twice in the leg by live bullets in Gaza rioting. He was in moderate condition.
French photographer Monoocher Deghati from AFP was wounded in the leg when hit by sniper fire.
"He was shot by a sniper by a live bullet," said a Reuters photographer who witnessed the incident.

Two other PBC journalists were lightly wounded near Ramallah on Thursday. Cameraman Abdel Nasser took a rubber bullet to the head and driver Ali Shanan was hit in the face by a rubber bullet, PBC said.
Cameraman Majdi Arabid of Britain's Worldwide Television News was lightly wounded when hit in the hand by rubber bullet, WTN said.
In Wednesday's clashes near Ramallah, four other PBC journalists were lightly wounded by rubber bullets.
PBC named the four as cameraman Abdel Karim Zeneid, driver Ghassan Kandah, cameraman Murad Siyam and reporter Ahmad Kaddoumi.
